prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the near-field 3D layout of the ego-vehicle cabin from the front right passenger seat, showing the upper roofline and A-pillars closest to the camera wearer (brightest white, ~0.3–0.5 m), the rearview mirror above left (~0.5 m), the dashboard and center console in front and below (~0.5–0.8 m, within arm's reach), the steering wheel to the left (~0.7–0.9 m, within the out-of-view driver's reach), and the right side-view mirror housing through the right window (~0.8 m). Across the five frames, the cabin surfaces stay at fixed distances relative to the wearer until frame 5, when the camera turns and tilts slightly downward to the left, bringing more of the steering wheel and the driver's lap and right hand (~0.6–0.8 m away at the bottom-left edge) into view. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map makes the recessed contours of the dark dashboard, steering wheel rim, and protruding mirror housings much easier to distinguish despite the dim cabin lighting. However, the map is highly unreliable for the exterior street scene occluded behind the rain-speckled glass, collapsing the road, buildings, the red car (~10–20 m ahead), and the motorcyclist (~10–15 m ahead to the right, ~3–4 m right of the red car and facing away) into an almost uniform black void with only faint, indistinct dark silhouettes.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map labels the surrounding ego-vehicle cabin (0.3–1.0 m away, with the dashboard and console within arm's reach below) as a large 'car' region while isolating a horizontal band of exterior vehicles seen through the windshield at roughly 10–50 m distance. It consistently tracks the red hatchback directly ahead in the left lane (cyan mask, ~10–20 m away, facing away from the camera wearer) alongside a row of oncoming and adjacent cars to its left (green, red, blue, orange, and purple masks spaced roughly 2–5 m apart from each other at 15–50 m), and in frames 3–5 it detects a silver SUV on the right side of the road (dark green mask, ~15–25 m away, ~4–6 m right of the red car) as the ego-car advances and the camera pans slightly left in frame 5. This instance masking separates distant, rain-obscured, and partially occluded vehicles along the left median that blend into the wet road and foliage in the RGB image. However, the map is unreliable because its ego-car mask bleeds heavily across the wet windshield and sky, and it completely misses the motorcyclist riding 10–15 m ahead between the red car and the right-hand SUV, the orange roadside barrier on the right in frame 1 (~3–4 m away), and the driver's body parts at the lower-left frame boundary.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is nearly blank across all five frames, displaying only a single small, horizontally tilted yellow body skeleton on the middle-left of frame 1 and no magenta hand skeletons anywhere. In the RGB context, two people are actually present in or near the scene: the driver seated immediately to the left (~0.5–0.8 m away, facing forward away from the camera wearer, mostly cut off by the left frame edge except for their legs and hand reaching toward the lower center console within arm's reach in frame 5) and a motorcyclist riding 10–15 m ahead and slightly right (facing away from the camera wearer). Across frames 2 through 5, the pose map remains completely black even as the camera tilts down and left in frame 5 to reveal the driver's hand and lap in the lower-left foreground. Consequently, the pose map provides no useful spatial information beyond the RGB strip and is wholly unreliable here, hallucinating a sideways torso and limb structure over the rearview mirror and distant traffic on the left of frame 1 while failing to detect both the distant motorcyclist and the nearby driver's limbs.
